\textbf{Source.} Muñoz-Garcia \& Toro-Gonzalez (2019), \emph{Strategy and Game Theory: Practice Exercises with Answers}, Ch. 4, Exercise 12 ``Stackelberg Competition with 2, or 3 Firms'', pp.~185--186 {[}PDF 197--198{]}. Reproduced verbatim (statement only; the book's worked answer follows it).

\begin{quote}
Consider a Stackelberg model of output competition where firm 1 is the industry leader and firm 2 is the follower. Firms face a linear inverse demand curve \(p(Q) = 10 - Q\), where \(Q = q_1 + q_2\) denotes the aggregate output sold by both firms. In addition, consider that firms are cost symmetric, facing a common marginal cost of \(MC_i = 2\) for every firm \(i = \{1, 2\}\) and no fixed costs.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{(\alph{enumi})}
\item
  Find the equilibrium in this Stackelberg game.
\item
  Assume now that a new firm (firm 3) joins the industry, acting last (after firm 2 chooses its output). Find the equilibrium in this Stackelberg game. Compare your results with those in part (a). How is the output of firm 1 and 2 affected by firm 3's entry?
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
